_metadata.rubric: x04 rubric (natural-click standard + five content questions), 2026-10-19
_metadata.independence: I read only the instructions file and the input file x04b-rc-input.json; no other file, repository search, web or paid API was used.

hints.reason: Pooh is the famous bear, and Rabbit is a well-known Hundred Acre Wood friend, so both sides click through the Pooh cast.

pairs.pair_note: Clean character-cast clue; Rabbit is slightly less iconic than Piglet or Tigger but still broadly known.

hints.reason: Pooh is a bear, and ROBIN resolves to Christopher Robin, a nice 'oh' moment since the board word looks like the bird.

pairs.pair_note: Good misdirection: ROBIN reads as a bird until Christopher Robin lands.

hints.reason: Pooh is a bear and Tigger is a tiger, two of the most iconic Hundred Acre Wood animals.

pairs.pair_note: Strong, warm clue; Tigger makes the TIGER side instant.

hints.reason: Sonic the Hedgehog is defined by being blue and being fast, both core traits of the character.

pairs.pair_note: Easy but clean; Sonic's two defining traits.

hints.reason: Sonic is the blue hedgehog, and collecting golden rings is the signature mechanic of the games.

pairs.pair_note: Rings are well known to anyone who has seen the games; fair and pleasant.

hints.reason: BOOM via 'sonic boom' and FAST via Sonic the speedy hedgehog (and supersonic speed itself), a satisfying two-way click.

pairs.pair_note: Both readings of SONIC reinforce speed, so the click is very natural.

hints.reason: BOOM via the physics term 'sonic boom' and RING via the hedgehog's golden rings, a real double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Nice split between science and the video game.

hints.reason: BOOM via 'sonic boom' and VIDEO GAME via Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog; fair, though VIDEO GAME is a broad target.

pairs.pair_note: Bonus: 'Sonic Boom' is also a Sonic spin-off title, which tightens the link.

hints.reason: Boxers throw punches and a punch bowl is a party staple, a classic instant double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Textbook double meaning; one of the best in the batch.

hints.reason: BREAD via the very familiar 'garlic bread' and SMELL via garlic's notorious odor (garlic breath).

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair; the SMELL side is a property rather than a phrase, which keeps it from feeling mechanical.

hints.reason: BREAD via 'garlic bread' and VAMPIRE via the famous folklore that garlic repels vampires; the contrast is fun.

pairs.pair_note: Funny juxtaposition (a vampire's worst side dish).

hints.reason: VAMPIRE is instant via garlic folklore, but BULB reads as a light bulb and U.S. cooks usually say 'head of garlic', so the garlic-bulb side takes effort.

pairs.pair_note: True and defensible once explained, but the BULB side is weak for most players; genuinely close to PASS.

hints.reason: CHRISTMAS via Santa's elves and COOKIE via the Keebler elves' hollow-tree bakery, a familiar U.S. brand mascot.

pairs.pair_note: Keebler gives a fun second route; SANTA (milk and cookies) would also work, but ELF is more interesting.

hints.reason: CHRISTMAS via Santa's elves and EAR via the iconic pointy elf ears, both instantly pictured.

pairs.pair_note: Simple visual clue; pleasant rather than surprising.

hints.reason: COW via black-and-white Holstein spots and DICE via the spots (pips) on each face, a neat visual analogy.

pairs.pair_note: Cow print plus dice dots is a nice visual pairing.

hints.reason: DICE via pips and DEER via a spotted fawn (think Bambi); the deer side needs a beat because adult deer are unspotted, but it clicks.

pairs.pair_note: Slightly weaker than the ladybug/giraffe/cow SPOTS pairs; still fair.

hints.reason: DICE via pips and GIRAFFE via its famous brown spot pattern, both strong visual images.

pairs.pair_note: Solid visual analogy.

hints.reason: DICE via black pips and LADYBUG via its black spots; the two even look alike (black dots on a solid shell/face).

pairs.pair_note: Best of the SPOTS family: a ladybug genuinely resembles a die face.

hints.reason: DICE via pips and SUN via the well-known word 'sunspots'; the sun side takes a moment but is a real, familiar fact.

pairs.pair_note: SUN is the least visual of the SPOTS targets but 'sunspots' is common knowledge.

hints.reason: HONEY via Pooh's honey pots is instant, and DISNEY via the Disney Winnie the Pooh franchise is true though DISNEY is a broad umbrella target.

pairs.pair_note: Fair, but the DISNEY side is categorical rather than specific; flagged uncertain.

hints.reason: DWARF via the classic elves-and-dwarves fantasy pairing (Tolkien, D&D) and SANTA via his workshop elves.

pairs.pair_note: Both sides familiar; pleasant fantasy-meets-holiday split.

hints.reason: EAR via pointy elf ears and MOVIE via Will Ferrell's hugely popular 'Elf'; MOVIE is broad but the film is iconic.

pairs.pair_note: MOVIE is a generic target, but 'Elf' is a top-tier U.S. Christmas film.

hints.reason: EAR via pointy elf ears and SANTA via his elf helpers; easy and clean.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair.

hints.reason: EAR via pointy elf ears and TOY via elves building toys in Santa's workshop.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair.

hints.reason: FAST via Sonic's trademark speed and VIDEO GAME via Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog series.

pairs.pair_note: Straightforward and fair.

hints.reason: GIRAFFE via its spot pattern and SUN via 'sunspots'; the sun side needs a beat but is familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; SUN is the softer side.

hints.reason: HONEY via Pooh's honey pots and OWL via Owl, a recognizable member of the Hundred Acre Wood cast.

pairs.pair_note: Owl is a second-tier character but still widely known.

hints.reason: HONEY via Pooh's love of honey and PIG via Piglet, his best-known companion.

pairs.pair_note: Warm and instant once Piglet surfaces.

hints.reason: HONEY via Pooh's honey and WOOD via the Hundred Acre Wood, a well-known setting that gives a nice 'oh' moment.

pairs.pair_note: The setting link is a pleasant non-obvious second route.

hints.reason: LADYBUG via its black spots and SUN via 'sunspots'; one strong side and one familiar-but-softer side.

pairs.pair_note: Fine; same SUN softness as the other sunspot pairs.

hints.reason: MARRIAGE via the wedding ring (noun) and PHONE via a phone ringing (verb), an instant double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Classic noun/verb split; easy and satisfying.

hints.reason: PIANO via its 88 keys and TEST via the answer key, two clearly different senses of KEY.

pairs.pair_note: Clean double meaning; facts correct (88 keys).

hints.reason: PIE via the familiar 'key lime pie' and TEST via the answer key; both phrases are everyday U.S. usage.

pairs.pair_note: Half phrase-join, half double meaning; fair and pleasant.

hints.reason: SMELL via garlic's strong odor works, but POWDER via 'garlic powder' is a flat spice-jar join that GARLIC does not naturally summon, so the pairing feels mechanical.

pairs.pair_note: True but unsatisfying; POWDER more readily evokes baby powder or snow, and the pairing lacks a fun click.

hints.reason: PRESS via the garlic press, a garlic-specific kitchen gadget, and SMELL via garlic's strong odor; a modest but real click.

pairs.pair_note: Stronger than POWDER+SMELL because a garlic press is a distinctive object, but still on the easy/flat side; second opinion welcome.

hints.reason: RING via the golden rings Sonic collects and VIDEO GAME via Sega's Sonic series.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; both sides from the same game.

hints.reason: SALT via the familiar seasoning 'garlic salt' and VAMPIRE via garlic-repels-vampires folklore; the vampire side carries the fun.

pairs.pair_note: Garlic salt is common in U.S. kitchens; pleasant.

hints.reason: SATURN via its famous planetary rings and WEDDING via exchanged wedding rings; a lovely cosmic-meets-romantic split.

pairs.pair_note: One of the nicest in the batch.

hints.reason: SMELL via garlic's pungent odor and VAMPIRE via the garlic folklore; the two are linked in popular culture (vampires recoil from the stench).

pairs.pair_note: Best of the GARLIC pairs: both sides are things everyone knows about garlic.

hints.reason: TOY via Santa's toy-building elves and SYRUP via Buddy the Elf's maple-syrup spaghetti, a beloved scene that delights fans though non-viewers may miss it.

pairs.pair_note: Big payoff for anyone who has seen 'Elf'; the SYRUP side depends on that film memory, hence uncertain.

hints.reason: TIE via the bow tie and VIOLIN via the violin bow, a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent, instant double meaning.
